lexical_decisions.rationale: The first member has copular ᾖ, be, while only the second has λέγηται, be called; the main text preserves that distinction. Place in the first member is an understood predicate drawn from the second member, not an expressed Greek noun there. Its English brackets disclose this interpretive ellipsis, not a printed lacuna, recovered wording, or restoration of Greek. The surrounding comparison of opposites and the explicit place predicate in the second member favor the elliptical reading. A material non-elliptical alternative is so that what exists should not exist, while what does not exist is called place, potentially functioning as a paradoxical reductio. That existential reading remains available; the main preference does not disprove it. Ceases to exist is not offered as that alternative because it would introduce a temporal change absent from μὴ ᾖ.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ οὗ ἂν αὐτοῦ μέρους λαμπρὸν γένηται, ὡς νεκρούμενον ψύχεται
lexical_decisions.chosen: wherever a part of it becomes bright, it grows cold as though dying
lexical_decisions.rationale: The supplied wording says bright, not dark. The resulting physical description is puzzling, but the main text preserves that printed adjective rather than silently emending it to fit the argument. Its referent is understood as a part of the air.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὴν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ μετουσίαν ἀπείρως ἐκτεταμένην ἔχειν
lexical_decisions.chosen: from having the presence proceeding from him extended infinitely
lexical_decisions.rationale: μετουσία can be presence, participation, or communicated influence. Presence preserves the analogy with the bounded sun’s effects without adding a second bodily substance.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὃ ἂν καὶ αὐτοῦ πληροῦν τὸ κενόν
lexical_decisions.chosen: which would also fill the void there
lexical_decisions.rationale: Takes αὐτοῦ locatively, there, referring to the discussed place or region. It is not nominative emphatic αὐτό, itself. A genitive alternative is which would also fill its void, with the precise possessive referent drawn from the surrounding body/region discussion; no replacement Greek is adopted.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τί οὖν ἔτι κωλύει τὸν θεὸν ὡς τούτου καὶ πάντων δημιουργὸν καὶ δεσπότην ὄντα, αὐτὸν μὲν ἐν σχήματι καὶ μορφῇ καὶ κάλλει ὄντα, τὴν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ μετουσίαν ἀπείρως ἐκτεταμένην ἔχειν;
lexical_decisions.chosen: What, then, still prevents God, as the maker and master of this and all things, while he himself has shape, form, and beauty, from having the presence proceeding from him extended infinitely?
lexical_decisions.rationale: The participial descriptions present God as maker/master and as himself being in shape, form, and beauty. The infinitive governed by prevents concerns his having the presence proceeding from him infinitely extended. The revised question preserves that grammatical focus rather than making the shape itself the prevented action and the extension merely circumstantial.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐ κατὰ κέλευσιν τὰς ἀποδείξεις ὑμῖν τοῦ οὕτως ἔχειν ἀνάγκη παρέχειν
lexical_decisions.chosen: Proofs that this is so must be supplied to you, not on the basis of a command.
lexical_decisions.rationale: The main text gives οὐ narrow scope over κατὰ κέλευσιν, leaving the obligation ἀνάγκη παρέχειν affirmative. The immediate placement of the negative before the command phrase favors this source-transparent scope, and the following developed proofs fit an obligation to supply demonstration rather than an appeal to command. A materially different broad scope denies obligation on command: We are not obliged to provide you at a command with proofs that things are so. The latter is a possible contextual construal, but the main text does not insert a negative before ἀνάγκη or claim the two scopes are equivalent. The source does not identify whose command is meant.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πλὴν αὐτὸ τὸ σκεῦος κενὸν ὂν οὐκ αὐτό ἐστι τόπος, ἀλλ’ ἐν ᾧ ἐστὶν αὐτὸ τὸ κενόν, εἴπερ σκεῦός ἐστιν.
lexical_decisions.chosen: Yet the vessel itself, being empty, is not itself place; rather, place is that in which the void itself is, if indeed it is a vessel.
lexical_decisions.rationale: The main text renders substantival αὐτὸ τὸ κενόν as the void itself, preserving the recurring κενόν earlier called void and tested hypothetically as a vessel. If indeed it is a vessel retains that conditional uncertainty rather than affirming that the void is a physical container. A contextual ellipsis can instead supply vessel from the preceding σκεῦος: Yet the vessel itself, being empty, is not itself place; rather, if it is a vessel, place is that in which the empty vessel itself is. The final vessel proviso supports that alternative, but the repeated substantive void is more source-transparent and no unprinted second vessel noun is required. The precise conditional referent remains open between the hypothesized void/container and the vessel already under discussion.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οἷον οὐρανός, γῆ, ὕδωρ, ἀὴρ καὶ εἰ ἄλλο τι ἐστὶν σῶμα
lexical_decisions.chosen: such as heaven, earth, water, air, and any other body, if there is one
lexical_decisions.rationale: The final item retains the separate καὶ εἰ existential condition, if there is another body, not merely an open-ended or-list. The following relative clause remains attached to the body/region discussion, including its existing locative-versus-genitive αὐτοῦ alternatives.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦτο γὰρ αὐτῷ (τὸ οὐδέν) οἰκειότερον ὄνομα
lexical_decisions.chosen: For ‘nothing’ is a more suitable name for it.
lexical_decisions.rationale: Quotation marks identify nothing as the proposed name in the source’s parenthesis τὸ οὐδέν, not an indefinite denial that any suitable name exists. For explicitly preserves the explanatory γάρ; more suitable retains the comparative οἰκειότερον.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πῶς δὲ καὶ πανταχῇ εἶναι δύναται, ἐν σχήματι ὤν;
lexical_decisions.chosen: And how can he also be everywhere while having a shape?
lexical_decisions.rationale: And retains the discourse link δέ and also separately preserves the additive καί introducing the further everywhere claim. The shape condition is unchanged.

lexical_decisions.chosen: And if the sun is absent from it, the air is enveloped in darkness
lexical_decisions.rationale: κἄν contracts καὶ ἐάν; and if preserves the link and conditional force rather than giving only temporal when. The subject shift is contextual: the sun is absent, while the air is enveloped in darkness. An even if emphasis is possible for the contracted particle, but the sequential account of the sun’s effects favors and if here; no absent Greek word or changed print is introduced.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὑπὸ δὲ τῆς αὐτοῦ ἀνατολῆς πάλιν φωτίζεται
lexical_decisions.chosen: But by the sun’s rising it is illuminated again
lexical_decisions.rationale: By makes the causal or agency force of ὑπό explicit, not only temporal coincidence at the rising. But and again retain δέ and πάλιν; the air remains the contextual subject.

passages.text: There is therefore one true God, who sits presiding in a superior form, being twice the heart of what is above and below. From him, as from a center, a substance wells forth with vital, incorporeal power and passes through all things, together with stars and the things belonging only to heaven, air, water, earth, fire, and anything else that exists. It is infinite in height, unbounded in depth, immeasurable in breadth, extending in three directions to infinity the life-giving and intelligent nature proceeding from him. This reality that proceeds from him and is infinite on every side must therefore have as its heart the one who truly is above all in shape. Wherever he may be, he is in the middle, as in something infinite, being the boundary of the whole. Therefore the extensions, beginning from him, have a nature drawn from what is boundless. Of these, one takes its beginning from him and reaches into height above, another into depth below, another to the right, another to the left, another in front, and another behind. Looking toward these as a number equal on every side, he completes the world in six intervals of time, himself being rest and having the coming boundless age as an image, being beginning and end. For the six infinities terminate in him and receive from him their extension into infinity.

source_issues.source_quote: σὺν τε ἄστροις καὶ μόνοις οὐρανοῦ, ἀέρος, ὕδατος, γῆς, πυρὸς
source_issues.issue: The relation of substantival μόνοις to the following element genitives is compressed. The main rendering understands things belonging only to those elements, preserving every supplied element and the only restriction; no conjectural replacement is adopted.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦ ἄνω τε καὶ κάτω δὶς ὑπάρχων καρδία
lexical_decisions.chosen: being twice the heart of what is above and below
lexical_decisions.rationale: δὶς literally means twice. Its precise link to above and below is compressed; the main text retains twice rather than replacing it with an unprinted cosmological term.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: σὺν τε ἄστροις καὶ μόνοις οὐρανοῦ, ἀέρος, ὕδατος, γῆς, πυρὸς
lexical_decisions.chosen: together with stars and the things belonging only to heaven, air, water, earth, fire
lexical_decisions.rationale: The adjective μόνοις is taken substantivally with an implicit things, qualified by the following genitives. The phrase is syntactically compressed; the main text preserves its only restriction and the complete element list, without changing μόνοις to another conjectured word.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐσία ἄπειρος εἰς ὕψος, ἀπέραντος εἰς βάθος, ἀμέτρητος εἰς πλάτος
lexical_decisions.chosen: a substance ... infinite in height, unbounded in depth, immeasurable in breadth
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the three distinct spatial measures and their distinct adjectives.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀνάγκη εἶναι καρδίαν, ἔχον τὸν ὄντως ὑπὲρ πάντα ἐν σχήματι
lexical_decisions.chosen: must ... have as its heart the one who truly is above all in shape
lexical_decisions.rationale: Takes εἶναι with ἔχον as a having construction, καρδίαν as what is had, and the person as its identifying complement. A more formally segmented rendering is must be a heart, containing the one, but the center-and-extensions argument favors having him as heart.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸν ἐσόμενον ἄπειρον αἰῶνα εἰκόνα ἔχων
lexical_decisions.chosen: having the coming boundless age as an image
lexical_decisions.rationale: Keeps the future age and image relationship without substituting an unprinted doctrine of the seventh day.

passages.text: This is the mystery of the sevenfold order. For he himself is the rest of all things, so that to those who imitate his greatness on a small scale he grants himself as rest. He alone is in one respect graspable and in another ungraspable, in one respect bounded and in another unbounded, having the extensions from him reaching into infinity. For he is graspable and ungraspable, near and far, being here and there, existing alone and possessing the communicating presence of the mind that is infinite on every side. By breathing this, the souls of all have life. Even if they are separated from the body, if they are found to possess longing for him, they are carried immortal into his embrace, just as in winter the vapors of the mountains, drawn by the sun’s rays, are carried toward the sun. What affection, then, can we conceive if we behold the beauty of his form with our mind? Otherwise it is impossible: for beauty cannot exist without form, nor can anyone be drawn toward love of him or even imagine seeing God if he has no form.

lexical_decisions.chosen: mystery of the sevenfold order
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἑβδομάς is a group of seven or a week. Sevenfold order retains the six extensions plus rest discussed just before; mystery of the week is a viable more familiar alternative.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦ πανταχόθεν ἀπείρου νοὸς τὴν μετουσίαν ἔχων
lexical_decisions.chosen: possessing the communicating presence of the mind that is infinite on every side
lexical_decisions.rationale: μετουσία can be participation, presence, or shared influence. Communicating presence retains its life-imparting reach in the breathing clause, without silently identifying a second deity.

lexical_decisions.chosen: they are carried ... into his embrace
lexical_decisions.rationale: κόλπος is bosom or lap; embrace makes the intimate image readable while retaining a personal destination.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὡς ἐν χειμῶνι ὥρας οἱ ἀτμοὶ τῶν ὀρῶν
lexical_decisions.chosen: just as in winter the vapors of the mountains
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the vapor simile and its mountain origin, without a modern scientific correction.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰς τὸν αὐτοῦ κόλπον φέρονται, ὡς ἐν χειμῶνι ὥρας οἱ ἀτμοὶ τῶν ὀρῶν ὑπὸ τῶν τοῦ ἡλίου ἀκτίνων ἑλκόμενοι φέρονται πρὸς αὐτὸν ἀθάνατοι.
lexical_decisions.chosen: they are carried immortal into his embrace, just as in winter the vapors of the mountains, drawn by the sun’s rays, are carried toward the sun
lexical_decisions.rationale: The main text attaches immortal to the souls because the paragraph concerns their continued life after separation from the body. ἀθάνατοι can grammatically agree with feminine souls or masculine vapors, and its printed position after the simile permits the local alternative the vapors ... are carried toward the sun, immortal. Moving the adjective to the souls is a disclosed attachment choice, not uniquely established by morphology.

passages.text: But some, being strangers to the truth and allies of evil, say under the pretext of glorifying him that he is without shape, so that, being formless and without appearance, he may be visible to no one and thus not become an object of longing. For a mind that does not see God’s form is empty of him. How can someone even pray without having anyone in whom to take refuge or on whom to lean? Having nothing solid to meet it, the mind is thrown off its footing into a void. “Yes,” someone says, “one should not fear God, but love him.” I too say this. But a good conscience about every good deed will bring this about, and doing good arises from fear. “But fear,” he says, “stuns the soul.” Yet I say it does not stun it, but awakens it and turns it back. Perhaps it would rightly be said that one ought not to fear God if we human beings did not fear many other things—I mean plots from our fellows, as well as wild animals, creeping creatures, diseases, afflictions, demons, and countless other things. Let the one who demands that we not fear God rescue us from these, so that we need not fear them either. But if he cannot, why does he begrudge our being released from countless fears through one fear directed toward the just one, and becoming able through a little faith in him to remove countless afflictions from ourselves and others, while also expecting a reward of good things and, by doing no evil through fear of the God who sees everything, continuing in peace even in the present?

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀντιτυπίαν γὰρ οὐκ ἔχων εἰς κενὸν ἐκβαθρεύεται.
lexical_decisions.chosen: Having nothing solid to meet it, the mind is thrown off its footing into a void.
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀντιτυπία denotes resistance or solidity encountered; the spatial image of a supportless mind is retained rather than a modern psychological diagnosis.

lexical_decisions.chosen: awakens it and turns it back
lexical_decisions.rationale: The turning verb is kept distinct from the reorientation terminology for μετανοέω.

lexical_decisions.chosen: through a little faith in him
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the small/little qualification instead of adding great faith.

passages.text: Thus grateful servitude to the true master sets all the rest free. So if it is possible for someone not to sin without fearing God, let him not fear. For it is possible, through love for him, not to do what does not meet with his approval. For both fearing him is written and loving him is commanded, so that each person may use a medicine suited to his own constitution. One can therefore fear him because he is just. Whether you fear or love, then, do not sin. May someone who fears be able to master unlawful pleasures, not desire what belongs to others, practice love of humanity, exercise self-control, and act justly. For I see some whose fear of him is incomplete committing very many sins. Let us therefore fear God not only because he is just: for in mercy toward those who have been wronged he punishes those who have wronged them. As water extinguishes fire, so fear does away with desire for evils. The person who teaches fearlessness does not himself fear; and the person who does not fear does not believe that there will be a judgment, increases his desires, practices magic, and slanders others for the things he himself does.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἡ πρὸς τὸν ὄντως δεσπότην εὐγνώμων δουλεία
lexical_decisions.chosen: grateful servitude to the true master
lexical_decisions.rationale: δουλεία denotes bonded service or slavery. Servitude retains the paradox that subjection to the true master frees from other masters; grateful also allows well-disposed.

lexical_decisions.chosen: sets all the rest free
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the plural all the rest; the scope may be everyone else affected or all remaining people, rather than silently replacing it with a different direct object such as all fears.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πρὸς τὴν αὐτοῦ ἕκαστος κρᾶσιν ἐπιτηδείῳ χρήσηται φαρμάκῳ
lexical_decisions.chosen: may use a medicine suited to his own constitution
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the medicine/constitution analogy and different appropriate responses rather than deleting fear or love.

passages.text: Hearing this, Simon interrupted and said, “I know whom you are addressing with these things. But so that I do not myself spend time on things I do not wish by saying the same things to refute you, you promised to answer the matters set before us. You said that you had adequately understood your teacher’s teachings because you were present to see him by direct perception and hear him, and that no one else could have the like through a vision or an apparition. But I will show that this is false. Someone who hears a person directly is not entirely assured about what is said, for his mind can reason: perhaps the figure before me, being human, is lying. An apparition, however, as soon as it is seen, gives the one seeing it assurance that it belongs to divinity. Answer me about this first.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: a vision or an apparition
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὅραμα and ὀπτασία are kept distinguishable in this argument; direct perception represents ἐνάργεια, the opposed category.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μὴ ἄρα ψεύδεται (ἄνθρωπος ὢν) τὸ φαινόμενον.
lexical_decisions.chosen: perhaps the figure before me, being human, is lying
lexical_decisions.rationale: The neuter the appearing thing/figure is the source’s way of referring to the visible speaker, not necessarily a supernatural apparition in this clause.

passages.text: Peter said, “You proposed to speak to one point but answered another. For you proposed that someone is better able to understand more ...... by hearing from an apparition than, indeed, from direct perception ... But then you went on to persuade us that the person hearing from an apparition is more secure than the one hearing from direct perception itself. Indeed, this was why you asserted that you knew Jesus’ teachings more adequately than I, as someone who had heard the word from him through an apparition. Nevertheless I answer the point proposed at the beginning. Once the prophet has first given assurance that he is a prophet, he is securely believed concerning what he says directly; having first been recognized as truthful, he answers after being examined and questioned as the learner wishes. But someone who trusts an apparition, a vision, or a dream is in danger, for he does not know whom he trusts. It is possible that this is an evil demon or a deceptive spirit, pretending in its speech to be what it is not. If someone should wish to inquire who the one appearing is, the apparition can say whatever it wishes about itself. Thus, flashing like an evil being and remaining as long as it wishes, it is extinguished, without staying for the questioner’s examination as long as the questioner wanted. Someone who sees through dreams cannot even inquire about what he wishes, for the sleeper’s reasoning is not under his own control. This is why, though we desire to learn many things while awake, in a dream we ask about other things, or, without even asking, hear about things of no concern to us. On waking we are discouraged that we neither heard about nor examined what we desired to learn.”

source_issues.source_quote: μᾶλλον δύνασθαί τινα πλεῖον νοεῖν ...... παρ’ ὀπτασίας ἀκούοντα, ἢ γὰρ παρὰ τῆς ἐναργείας ...
source_issues.issue: Six dots and then three dots mark two printed gaps. Both exact counts remain, without restoring the missing wording or hiding the interrupted syntax.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μᾶλλον δύνασθαί τινα πλεῖον νοεῖν ...... παρ’ ὀπτασίας ἀκούοντα, ἢ γὰρ παρὰ τῆς ἐναργείας ...
lexical_decisions.chosen: someone is better able to understand more ...... by hearing from an apparition than, indeed, from direct perception ...
lexical_decisions.rationale: Better able separately represents μᾶλλον with δύνασθαι, while understand more represents πλεῖον with νοεῖν. Exactly six and three printed gap dots remain; no missing words are restored. The comparison is retained, with indeed representing γάρ in the interrupted construction.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the apparition can say whatever it wishes about itself
lexical_decisions.rationale: The subject of δύναται is unstated. The main text takes the apparition as subject, interpreting the dative as speaking on its own behalf, with self-description inferred from the preceding identity question. About itself is not claimed as the literal meaning of ἑαυτῷ. A materially different reading takes the questioner as subject and the reflexive as to himself: If someone wishes to inquire who the appearing figure is, he can tell himself whatever he wishes. The following evanescent apparition favors the main subject continuation, but does not eliminate the alternative.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἢ δαίμονα κακὸν εἶναι ἢ πνεῦμα πλάνον
lexical_decisions.chosen: an evil demon or a deceptive spirit
lexical_decisions.rationale: Both alternatives remain distinct.

passages.text: Simon said, “If you say that apparitions do not always speak truth, nevertheless visions and dreams, being sent by God, do not lie about whatever he wishes to say.” Peter said, “You said correctly that, being sent by God, they do not lie. But it is unclear whether the person who saw it has seen a God-sent dream.” Simon said, “If the person who saw it is righteous, he has seen something true.” Peter said, “You said correctly. But who is righteous if he needs a vision to learn what he ought to learn and to do what he ought to do?” Simon said, “Grant me this, that only the righteous person can see a true vision, and I will answer you on that point. For I have decided that an impious person does not see a true dream.” Peter said, “This is false, and I can demonstrate it both without writing and from writing, though I do not promise to persuade you. For a man who has inclined toward love of a wicked woman does not transfer his mind to lawful life together with another who is good in every way. Sometimes, even knowing in themselves which is better, because they are already captivated they love the worse one. You too are suffering something like this without knowing it.” Simon said, “Leave these things aside and speak to what you promised. For it seems impossible to me for impious people to be given dreams by God in any manner.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: both without writing and from writing
lexical_decisions.rationale: The contrast is between proof apart from written texts and proof from them, not between illiteracy and literacy.

lexical_decisions.chosen: because they are already captivated
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preoccupation or prior capture explains the persistence in an inferior attachment; no explicit compulsion beyond the source is added.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀλλ’ οὖν γε τὰ ὁράματα καὶ τὰ ἐνύπνια θεόπεμπτα ὄντα οὐ ψεύδεται, περὶ ὧν ἂν εἰπεῖν θέλῃ.
lexical_decisions.chosen: nevertheless visions and dreams, being sent by God, do not lie about whatever he wishes to say
lexical_decisions.rationale: He understands God as the subject of θέλῃ, chosen because God is the sender encoded in θεόπεμπτα. The subject is not expressly named. About whatever they wish to say is a material alternative with visions and dreams as subject, since a neuter plural can take a singular verb, as the immediately preceding ψεύδεται does. Neither reading requires correcting the supplied text.

passages.text: Peter said, “I remember that I promised to show this and supply proof both without writing and from writing. Now listen as I speak. We know many people—if you are fair-minded; in any case I have those present as judges—who revere idols, commit adultery, and sin in every way, yet see visions and true dreams, some even apparitions of demons. For I do not say that anyone can see the fleshless form of Father or Son, because mortal eyes are dazzled by the greatest light. Therefore God’s not being seen by the human being who has been turned into flesh is not because he begrudges it, but because he is merciful. For the one who sees cannot live. The excess of light dissolves the flesh of the viewer, unless by God’s ineffable power the flesh is transformed into the nature of light so that it can see light, or the substance of light is transformed into flesh so that it can be seen by flesh. For seeing the Father without transformation belongs to the Son alone. The righteous do not see in the same way: at the resurrection of the dead, when their bodies have been transformed into light and they become equal to angels, then they will be able to see. Indeed, even if one of the angels attempts to appear to a human being, he turns into flesh so that he can be seen by flesh. For no one can see a fleshless power, not only that of the Son but not even that of an angel. But if someone sees an apparition, let him understand it to be that of an evil demon.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the fleshless form
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains form without flesh, not shapelessness, since the argument distinguishes the two.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the human being who has been turned into flesh
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the transformation wording without replacing it with a philosophical assumption about human origins.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸ γὰρ ἀτρέπτως πατέρα ἰδεῖν υἱοῦ μόνου ἐστίν.
lexical_decisions.chosen: For seeing the Father without transformation belongs to the Son alone.
lexical_decisions.rationale: Without transformation can concern the conditions of the seeing encounter or the viewer/seen; English leaves the qualification unassigned rather than claiming explicitly which party remains unchanged.

lexical_decisions.chosen: equal to angels
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains equality to angels, not an assertion that human beings become angels.

passages.text: Nevertheless, that even impious people see true visions and dreams is clear, and I can prove it from writing. For it is written in the law that Abimelech—being impious and having wished to defile the wife of righteous Abraham through intercourse—heard from God in sleep, as the scripture says, not to touch her because she was living with a husband. Pharaoh too, an impious man, saw a dream about abundance and scarcity of wheat; Joseph, explaining it to him, said that the dream had come from God. Nebuchadnezzar, who revered idols and ordered those who revered God to be thrown into fire, saw a dream concerning an age’s whole length. And let no one say, “But no impious person beholds a vision while awake.” That is false. Nebuchadnezzar himself, after ordering three men to be thrown into fire, saw a fourth in the furnace and said, “I see the fourth as a son of God.” Yet although they saw true apparitions, visions, and dreams, they were impious. Such a person is not necessarily reverent simply because he sees visions, dreams, and apparitions. For to the reverent person truth wells up in an inborn and pure mind, not pursued through a dream, but given to good people through understanding.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸν τέταρτον ὁρῶ ὡς υἱὸν θεοῦ
lexical_decisions.chosen: I see the fourth as a son of God
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the anarthrous son of God in the quoted statement without identifying the figure as a particular later doctrinal person.

lexical_decisions.chosen: a dream concerning an age’s whole length
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the broad age-duration wording rather than identifying an unprinted historical timetable.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῷ γὰρ εὐσεβεῖ ἐμφύτῳ καὶ καθαρῷ ἀναβλύζει τῷ νῷ τὸ ἀληθές
lexical_decisions.chosen: to the reverent person truth wells up in an inborn and pure mind
lexical_decisions.rationale: The adjectival grouping can also be taken as in the reverent, inborn, and pure mind; both emphasize inward truth and do not make the dream the source of it.

lexical_decisions.chosen: saw a fourth in the furnace and said
lexical_decisions.rationale: τέταρτον remains the object of seeing in the narrator’s construction, not merely the subject matter of the subsequent speaking. The following quotation is retained as a separate reported statement.

passages.text: For this is how the Son was revealed to me too by the Father. Therefore I know the power of revelation, having learned from my own experience. For as soon as the Lord asked who people said he was, and I had heard different people saying different things about him, it rose in my heart. I do not know, then, how I said, “You are the Son of the living God.” He pronounced me blessed and told me that the one who had revealed it was the Father. From then on I learned that learning without being taught, without an apparition or dreams, is revelation. And this truly is so. For in the thing placed within us by God in seed form ...., all truth resides. It is covered and uncovered by God’s hand, the one who brings this about knowing what accords with each person’s worth. But that something is made known from outside through apparitions and dreams is plainly not a matter of revelation but of anger. Indeed, it is written in the law that God, angry with Aaron and Miriam, said, “If a prophet arises from among you, through visions and dreams I will make myself known to him; but not in this way as with Moses my servant, because I will speak to him in visible form and not through dreams, as someone will speak to his own friend.” You see how the things of anger come through visions and dreams, whereas those addressed to a friend are mouth to mouth, in visible form, and not through riddles, visions, and dreams as to an enemy.

source_issues.source_quote: ἐν γὰρ τῇ ἐν ἡμῖν ἐκ θεοῦ τεθείσῃ σπερματικῶς....
source_issues.issue: The four-dot printed gap leaves a noun or additional wording unavailable. Exactly four dots remain, and thing is only generic English grammatical support, not an identification or recovery of the lost content.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐν γὰρ τῇ ἐν ἡμῖν ἐκ θεοῦ τεθείσῃ σπερματικῶς....
lexical_decisions.chosen: For in the thing placed within us by God in seed form ....
lexical_decisions.rationale: Exactly four gap dots remain. Thing is generic English nominal support for the surviving article/participle; it does not identify the unavailable noun or restore a specific faculty.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: θεοῦ δὲ χειρὶ σκέπεται καὶ ἀποκαλύπτεται
lexical_decisions.chosen: It is covered and uncovered by God’s hand
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the cover/uncover opposition underlying revelation rather than describing only disclosure.

lexical_decisions.chosen: Moses my servant
lexical_decisions.rationale: θεράπων is an attendant or servant; the wording is retained without importing a different familiar biblical quotation.

lexical_decisions.chosen: in visible form
lexical_decisions.rationale: εἶδος is appearance or form, fitting the contrast with dream and riddle. Directly is a looser alternative that would obscure the explicit form-language.

passages.text: If, then, our Jesus also appeared to you through a vision, was made known, and conversed with you, it was as with an adversary, in anger. That is why he spoke through visions and dreams, or even through revelations that come from outside. But can anyone become wise for teaching through an apparition? If you say, “It is possible,” why did the teacher spend an entire year staying with people who were awake and conversing with them? And how shall we even believe you about the very claim that he appeared to you? How did he appear to you, when you think the opposite of his teaching? But if, after being seen and instructed by him for a single hour, you became an apostle, proclaim his words, explain his teachings, love his apostles, and do not fight me, who lived with him. For you have stood against me as an enemy, when I am a solid rock, a foundation of an assembly. If you were not an adversary, you would not, by slandering me, revile the proclamation that comes through me, so that I should not be believed when I say what I myself heard from the Lord while present—that is, as though I had been condemned and were unapproved. Or if you call me “condemned,” you accuse the God who revealed the Messiah to me and attack the one who pronounced me blessed on account of revelation. But if you truly wish to cooperate with the truth, first learn from us what we learned from him, and, becoming a disciple of truth, become our fellow worker.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὑπ’ ἐκείνου μιᾶς ὥρας ὀφθεὶς καὶ μαθητευθεὶς
lexical_decisions.chosen: after being seen and instructed by him for a single hour
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the passive being seen by him rather than silently reversing it into seeing him. The hour qualifies the short encounter and instruction.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: στερεὰν πέτραν ὄντα με, θεμέλιον ἐκκλησίας
lexical_decisions.chosen: when I am a solid rock, a foundation of an assembly
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains Peter’s self-description as rock/foundation. Church is a conventional alternative for ἐκκλησία, but the Greek does not specify a later institution.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the Messiah
lexical_decisions.rationale: Uses the POB title rendering because χριστός here functions independently, not in a personal-name construction.

lexical_decisions.chosen: “condemned”
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the marked quoted verdict without identifying an unnamed opponent with a historical person not named in this section.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: δηλονότι ὡς ἐμοῦ καταγνωσθέντος καὶ ἐμοῦ ἀδοκίμου ὄντος
lexical_decisions.chosen: —that is, as though I had been condemned and were unapproved
lexical_decisions.rationale: δηλονότι introduces an explanatory statement of the alleged grounds for withholding belief. That is preserves its scope outside the supposed condemnation rather than saying that condemnation itself was clear.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: διὰ τί ὅλῳ ἐνιαυτῷ ἐγρηγορόσιν παραμένων ὡμίλησεν ὁ διδάσκαλος;
lexical_decisions.chosen: why did the teacher spend an entire year staying with people who were awake and conversing with them?
lexical_decisions.rationale: The entire-year duration qualifies the teacher’s staying and conversing, not the duration of the listeners’ wakefulness. Spend an entire year expresses the temporal dative, staying represents παραμένων, and conversing preserves ὡμίλησεν. Awake remains the listeners’ state in contrast with a dream encounter, without a claim of uninterrupted yearlong wakefulness.

passages.text: Hearing this, Simon said, “Far be it from me to become a disciple either of him or of you. For I am not ignorant of what must be known. What I asked about as though learning was so that I might know whether you can show evidence to be more evident than an apparition. But you spoke as you wished; you did not demonstrate it. And now, tomorrow, I will come and speak with you on the subject of God, whom you insist is the maker, and show that he is not the highest and good. I will also show that your teacher said the same things as I, and expose you as not having understood.” After saying this, he went out, unwilling to hear an answer to the matters he had proposed.

lexical_decisions.chosen: show evidence to be more evident than an apparition
lexical_decisions.rationale: Evidence/evident preserves the visible repetition of ἐνάργεια/ἐναργεστέρα. Evidence here denotes manifest direct encounter, the direct-perception category contrasted earlier with apparition, not documentary or syllogistic proof. ὀπτασίας is taken as the comparative genitive, than an apparition, because Simon asks whether Peter can establish the superiority of direct encounter. The material possessive alternative takes it with ἐνάργειαν: show more evident manifestation of an apparition, with the comparison left implicit. Neither attachment is a correction to the printed Greek.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μὴ αὐτὸν εἶναι ἀνώτατον καὶ ἀγαθόν
lexical_decisions.chosen: that he is not the highest and good
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the coordinated predicate under the negative without silently splitting it into two independent categorical denials.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: σὺ δὲ ὡς ἠθέλησας εἶπες, οὐχ ἔδειξας.
lexical_decisions.chosen: But you spoke as you wished; you did not demonstrate it.
lexical_decisions.rationale: As represents the manner expressed by ὡς, not an object meaning whatever content you wished. The contrasting failure to demonstrate remains explicit.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ τὸν σὸν δὲ διδάσκαλον τὰ αὐτά μοι εἰρηκέναι
lexical_decisions.chosen: I will also show that your teacher said the same things as I
lexical_decisions.rationale: Takes μοι as a dative of comparison with the same things, because Simon proposes to prove the teacher’s agreement with his asserted position against Peter’s interpretation. The same things to me is a material alternative taking μοι as recipient of said; the main rendering does not claim that Simon’s receipt of teaching is grammatically excluded.

passages.text: At dawn, when Peter came forward to converse, Simon spoke first: “As I left yesterday, I promised you that today I would return, debate with you, and show that the one who fashioned the world is not the highest God, but another, who alone is good and has remained unknown until now. To begin, then: do you say that the maker himself is also lawgiver, or not? If he is lawgiver, he is just; and being just, he is not good. If he is not good, Jesus proclaimed another when he said, ‘Do not call me good, for the good one is one, the Father in the heavens.’ This does not agree with the lawgiver’s being both just and good.” Peter said, “First tell us: on account of what actions does the good one seem to you good, and on account of what actions the just one just? In this way we can aim our arguments at the target.” Simon said, “You tell me first: what do you think goodness is? Or justice, too?”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: δίκαιος δὲ ὢν ἀγαθὸς οὐκ ἔστιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: being just, he is not good
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains Simon’s opposition of justice and goodness as his claim, not the translator’s conclusion.

lexical_decisions.chosen: aim our arguments at the target
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the aiming/target image.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: Σὺ πρῶτον εἰπὲ τί σοι δοκεῖ τὸ ἀγαθόν; ἢ καὶ τὸ δίκαιον;
lexical_decisions.chosen: You tell me first: what do you think goodness is? Or justice, too?
lexical_decisions.rationale: The substantival good and just are rendered as goodness and justice. Or ... too preserves the second question’s disjunctive and additive ἢ καί rather than replacing both questions with one and-linked list.

passages.text: Peter said, “So that I do not spend time in a more contentious debate, rightly demanding that you answer my questions, I will give the answers as you wish, although I was the one who asked. I say that the good person is the one who provides, as I see the maker himself doing when he provides the sun to good and evil people and rain to the righteous and unrighteous.” Simon said, “This is most unjust: he provides the same things to the righteous and unrighteous.” Peter said, “Then you tell us from now on how he would act to be good.” Simon said, “You must say.” Peter said, “I will. If, by providing the same things to the good and righteous and also to the evil and unrighteous, he is according to you not even just, and if, by providing good things to the good and bad things to the bad, you would reasonably call him just, what further course of action could he take, if not this way: providing temporary things to the evil, in case they change, and eternal things to the good, provided they remain? Thus, in providing for all but granting favors to different recipients, his justice is good and all the more patient in this respect, if he forgives the sins of sinners who reorient and also promises eternal life to those who have acted well. But in judging at the end and assigning to each what is deserved, he is just. If, then, these matters rightly stand this way, acknowledge it; but if they do not seem right to you, refute them.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: the one who provides
lexical_decisions.rationale: Goodness is defined through giving/provision in this argument; generous is an alternative, but provision is kept explicit.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἁμαρτωλοῖς μὲν μετανοοῦσιν χαρίζεται τὰ ἁμαρτήματα
lexical_decisions.chosen: he forgives the sins of sinners who reorient
lexical_decisions.rationale: Uses POB reorientation wording, traditionally repent, preserving forgiveness and its relation to the response. Who reorient renders the participle; the encompassing if is separately retained for the printed εἰ.

lexical_decisions.chosen: promises eternal life
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὑπογράφω can pledge, prescribe, or outline. Promises fits the positive undertaking to those who act well, without claiming automatic possession already.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὡς σοὶ δοκεῖ αὐτὸς ὢν ἐπυθόμην ποιήσομαι τὰς· ἀποκρίσεις.
lexical_decisions.chosen: I will give the answers as you wish, although I was the one who asked.
lexical_decisions.rationale: The supplied construction juxtaposes participial ὢν with finite ἐπυθόμην irregularly. The English reads this contextually as Peter answering despite having himself asked. A relative ὃς in place of printed ὢν would support a smoother clause but would be conjectural; it is not substituted. The supplied stop between article and noun in τὰς· ἀποκρίσεις is a print punctuation feature, not an alleged OCR defect.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῷ μὲν πᾶσιν παρέχειν, διαφόροις δὲ χαρίζεσθαι
lexical_decisions.chosen: in providing for all but granting favors to different recipients
lexical_decisions.rationale: διαφόροις is taken as a dative of recipients, contrasting everyone with differentiated beneficiaries. It can also mean distinguished or worthy recipients; the main text leaves the difference unspecified. The previous different-gifts rendering would require an instrumental interpretation, by differing gifts, rather than an accusative object; that is a material alternative but the recipient reading is more direct with χαρίζεσθαι.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ μακρόθυμον ταύτη μᾶλλον, εἰ ἁμαρτωλοῖς μὲν μετανοοῦσιν χαρίζεται τὰ ἁμαρτήματα, εὖ πράξασιν δὲ καὶ ζωὴν αἰώνιον ὑπογράφει.
lexical_decisions.chosen: and all the more patient in this respect, if he forgives the sins of sinners who reorient and also promises eternal life to those who have acted well.
lexical_decisions.rationale: If preserves εἰ governing the argument through both forgiveness and the promise of life. The participle who reorient is distinct from that condition; the sentence is not changed into an unconditional assertion by a colon.

passages.text: Simon said, “I have said it once: every lawgiver, looking toward what is just, is just.” Peter said, “If it belongs to goodness not to lay down a law, and to justice to lay one down, even in this way the maker is both good and just: good because, from Adam’s time until Moses, he does not appear to have laid down the law in writing; and from Moses down to the present times, as it is written, he is also just.” Simon said, “Show from your teacher’s statements that it belongs to the same one to be good and just. For it seems impossible to me that the lawgiver, being good, is himself also just.” Peter said, “Listen to how the good itself is also just. Our teacher himself, when the Pharisee said, ‘What must I do to inherit eternal life?’ first said, ‘Do not call me good, for the good one is one, the Father in the heavens.’ Immediately afterward he added, ‘But if you wish to enter life, keep the commandments.’ When the man said, ‘Which ones?’ he directed him to those of the law. Had he been indicating someone else as good, he would not have referred him to the commandments of the just one. I myself also acknowledge that what is just is one thing and what is good another; but you do not know that being good and just belong to the same one. For he is good in being patient now with those who reorient and receiving them; and he is just when, in judging, he assigns to each what is deserved.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐγγράφως οὐ φαίνεται τεθεικὼς τὸν νόμον
lexical_decisions.chosen: he does not appear to have laid down the law in writing
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the in-writing qualification and appears, not an absolute claim that there was no divine instruction before Moses.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the Pharisee
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the source’s identification of the questioner rather than harmonizing it to a different designation in a familiar Gospel account.

lexical_decisions.chosen: those who reorient
lexical_decisions.rationale: Uses POB reorientation terminology, traditionally those who repent, without an unprinted intensifier.

passages.text: Simon said, “How, then, when the maker was known—the one who formed Adam and was known to the righteous according to the law, and furthermore to the righteous and unrighteous and the whole world—does your teacher, coming after all those people, say, ‘No one knew the Father except the Son, just as no one knows the Son except the Father and those to whom the Son wishes to reveal him’? He would not have said these things unless he were announcing a certain Father who is in secrecy, whom the law also calls Most High, from whom no good or evil utterance has been heard, as Jeremiah too testifies in the Lamentations. In accordance with the number of the sons of Israel who entered Egypt, who are seventy, and marking out the nations’ boundaries by seventy languages, this one gave the Hebrews as a portion to his Son, who is also called Lord and ordered heaven and earth, and appointed him God of gods. By gods I mean those who have received the other portions of the nations. Laws therefore issued from all the gods just mentioned to their own portions, namely the remaining nations; likewise the law established among the Hebrews issued from the Son, the Lord of all. It was determined to be this way so that if someone takes refuge in someone’s law, he becomes part of the portion of the one whose law he has undertaken to practice. No one knew the Most High Father who is in secrecy, just as no one knew of this one’s Son that he is Son. Indeed, you, assigning to the Son the distinctive attributes of the secret Most High, do not know that he is Son, being Father of the Jesus whom you call Messiah.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: in secrecy
lexical_decisions.rationale: The expression can mean among unrevealed mysteries or in the secret realm. In secrecy preserves the hidden status without inventing a named location.

lexical_decisions.chosen: In accordance with the number of the sons of Israel
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains Israel, not another textual witness’s sons of God or angels; the explicit count seventy remains.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῷ αὐτοῦ υἱῷ τῷ καὶ „κυρίῳ“ λεγομένῳ
lexical_decisions.chosen: to his Son, who is also called Lord
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains Simon’s distinction between the Most High and his Son, who is the maker in this proposal, not the translator’s own theological identification.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ καθ’ ὑμᾶς λεγομένου χριστοῦ
lexical_decisions.chosen: the Jesus whom you call Messiah
lexical_decisions.rationale: χριστός is a disputed independent title attributed by Simon to the other party’s Jesus, so Messiah preserves the title’s force.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὅστις κατὰ ἀριθμὸν τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ, οἳ εἰσῆλθον εἰς Αἴγυπτον (οἵ εἰσιν ἑβδομήκοντα), καὶ πρὸς τὰ ὅρια τῶν ἐθνῶν περιγράψας γλώσσαις ἑβδομήκοντα
lexical_decisions.chosen: In accordance with the number of the sons of Israel who entered Egypt, who are seventy, and marking out the nations’ boundaries by seventy languages
lexical_decisions.rationale: The object of περιγράψας is implicit. The English takes the boundaries named in πρὸς τὰ ὅρια as the contextual object of marking out, not as a direct Greek accusative object outside the preposition. A more formally separated alternative is having marked out divisions by seventy languages in accordance with that number and in relation to the nations’ boundaries. Both number and boundary expressions constrain the delineation; no additional printed noun is claimed.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀπὸ τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ πάντων κυρίου
lexical_decisions.chosen: from the Son, the Lord of all
lexical_decisions.rationale: Takes the second genitive phrase appositionally, since the Son was already explicitly called Lord in this proposal. From the Son of the Lord of all is a material alternative attaching the second genitive as the Son’s parent; the main text does not claim the appositional grouping is uniquely settled.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐδεὶς ἔγνω τὸν ἐν ἀπορρήτοις ὕψιστον πατέρα ὄντα, ὡς οὐδὲ τὸν τούτου υἱὸν ὅτι υἱός ἐστιν.
lexical_decisions.chosen: No one knew the Most High Father who is in secrecy, just as no one knew of this one’s Son that he is Son.
lexical_decisions.rationale: The main text reads Father attributively as the identification of the hidden Most High, whose inaccessible status and unheard voice Simon has described. A material alternative takes πατέρα ὄντα predicatively: No one knew that the Most High who is in secrecy is Father, just as no one knew that his Son is Son. That alternative aligns the two clauses as failures to recognize paternal and filial identity rather than knowledge of a person; the main reading is retained contextually, not claimed as unique.

passages.text: After Simon said these things, Peter said to him, “Can you call that very one to witness that you believe this—not the one you now say is in secrecy, but the one you believe in without acknowledging him? For you talk nonsense by defining one thing in place of another. Therefore, if you call him to witness that you believe what you say, I will answer you; but if you stand debating with me things you do not believe, you force me to strike at emptiness.” Simon said, “I heard from one of your disciples ....” Peter said, “Do not bear false witness.” Simon said, “Do not abuse me, you utterly rash man.” Peter said, “Until you name the person who said it, you are a liar.” Simon said, “Suppose that I invented these things, or even heard them from someone else: answer me about them. For if they cannot be overturned, I have learned that this is the truth.” Peter said, “If it is a human fabrication, I will not answer it. But if you have been gripped by the supposition that it is true, acknowledge this very thing to me, and I myself also have something to say about it.” Simon said, “Once for all, I think it is so. If you have anything to say about these things, answer.”

source_issues.source_quote: Παρὰ τινὸς τῶν σῶν μαθητῶν ἀκήκοα . . . .
source_issues.issue: Exactly four printed dots remain; the missing report is not reconstructed.

lexical_decisions.chosen: call ... to witness
lexical_decisions.rationale: The demand invokes the one actually believed in as witness, not a request for a merely informal reassurance.

lexical_decisions.chosen: strike at emptiness
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the striking-at-a-void metaphor.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: Παρὰ τινὸς τῶν σῶν μαθητῶν ἀκήκοα . . . .
lexical_decisions.chosen: I heard from one of your disciples ....
lexical_decisions.rationale: Exactly four dots remain for the printed gap; the alleged disclosure’s missing content is not restored.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰ δὲ ὑπονοίᾳ αὐτοῦ κεχράτησαι ὡς ἀληθοῦς
lexical_decisions.chosen: But if you have been gripped by the supposition that it is true
lexical_decisions.rationale: The selected reading has κεχράτησαι, interpreted contextually as passive holding or gripping. Regular κεκράτησαι is only a possible spelling regularization, not substituted or described as verified text. The English clarifies that the supposition concerns the account’s truth, while preserving the printed construction and its uncertainty.

passages.text: Peter said, “If this is so, you act with the greatest impiety. For if it belongs to the Son who ordered heaven and earth to reveal his Father who is in secret to whomever he wishes, you, as I said, act with the greatest impiety by revealing to those to whom he did not reveal.” Simon said, “But he himself wants me to reveal.” Peter said, “You do not understand what I say, Simon. Yet listen and understand. Saying, ‘To those to whom the Son wishes he will reveal,’ does not mean that someone learns such a thing by teaching, but only by revelation. Revelation is what lies secretly in all human hearts, covered, being uncovered without a voice expressing his will. Thus one comes to know not by being taught, but by understanding. Yet the one who has understood is not permitted to demonstrate this to another, since he himself was not taught; nor can he reveal it, since he himself is not the Son—unless he says that he himself is the Son. But you are not the standing Son. For if you were Son, you would certainly know those worthy of such revelation. But you do not know. For if you knew, you would do the things done by those who know.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἄνευ φωνῆς τῆς αὐτοῦ βουλῆς ἀποκαλυπτόμενον
lexical_decisions.chosen: being uncovered without a voice expressing his will
lexical_decisions.rationale: The genitive τῆς αὐτοῦ βουλῆς is attached to voice, a voice of his will, expressed readably as a voice expressing his will. It is not assigned independent instrumental force as by his will, for which the supplied genitive gives no established grammatical support. Nonvocal disclosure remains explicit.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the standing Son
lexical_decisions.rationale: Keeps the standing epithet and Son together, rather than replacing them with a later named title or deleting the unusual description.

lexical_decisions.chosen: his Father who is in secret
lexical_decisions.rationale: The secrecy phrase is attributive inside the Father noun phrase, not the manner in which the Son reveals him. Who is in secret makes this attachment explicit without specifying a named hidden realm.

passages.text: Simon said, “I admit I did not understand how you mean, ‘You would do the things done by those who know.’” Peter said, “If you did not understand, you also cannot know each person’s mind. And if you do not know, you also do not know those worthy of revelation. If you do not know, you are not Son; but the Son knows, and therefore reveals to those he wishes as being worthy.” Simon said, “Let me not deceive: I know those who are worthy, and I am not Son. Yet I did not understand what this is, ‘He reveals to those he wishes,’ as you say. I said that I did not understand not because I did not know, but because I knew that those present did not understand, so that you would state it more clearly and those for whose sake we also conduct the discussion might understand.” Peter said, “I cannot state it more clearly. Since you have understood it, explain it yourself.” Simon said, “I am not obliged to state your views.” Peter said, “It seems to me, Simon, that you do not understand it and are unwilling to admit it, lest, being caught in ignorance, you be exposed as not being the standing Son. For this is what you hint at, even if you do not wish to say it plainly. Thus I know your intentions from your hints, being a disciple of a true prophet, not a prophet. But you, though you do not understand even what is plainly said, wish to call yourself Son, standing against us.” Simon said, “I will remove every excuse from you. I admit that I did not understand what this is: ‘And to those to whom the Son wishes, he reveals.’ So state it more clearly.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: the standing Son
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the epithet tied to Simon’s alleged claim; it is not identified with an external historical person.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: προφήτου ἀληθοῦς μαθητὴς ὤν, οὐ προφήτης
lexical_decisions.chosen: being a disciple of a true prophet, not a prophet
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves Peter’s explicit denial of being a prophet in this statement, rather than harmonizing it to a later title.

lexical_decisions.chosen: Let me not deceive:
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀπατῶ is first-person singular, compatible with a first-person subjunctive here; let me not deceive preserves that person and the negative. The possible interrogative indicative alternative is Am I deceiving?, expecting a negative answer. The edition’s printed stop fits the chosen noninterrogative construction, but does not settle the form’s mood. No second-person imperative or replacement Greek is introduced.

passages.text: Peter said, “Since you have admitted, even if only for appearances, that you do not understand it, answer what I ask you, and you will learn. Tell me: do you say that the Son, whoever he may be, is just, or not?” Simon said, “Most just.” Peter said, “If he is just, why does he not reveal to all, but to those he wishes?” Simon said, “Because, being just, he wishes to reveal to those who are worthy.” Peter said, “Then must he not know each person’s mind so that he may reveal to the worthy?” Simon said, “It must certainly be so.” Peter said, “Then he alone was reasonably appointed to reveal, since he alone knows each person’s mind—not you, who cannot even understand the things we say.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: even if only for appearances
lexical_decisions.rationale: σχήματι can indicate outward form or pretense; even formally is a less interpretive alternative. The admission is treated skeptically, not accepted as sincere without qualification.

passages.text: After Peter said this, praise arose from the crowds. Simon, thoroughly exposed, blushed in shame, rubbed his forehead, and said, “But they call me a magician, defeated by Peter, and also caught in argument. Yet if someone is caught in argument and taken unawares, he does not thereby have the truth within him defeated; for the weakness of its defender is not the truth of the defeated party. Nevertheless I tell you that I judged everyone present worthy to know the Father who is in secret. Therefore, when I reveal him to them publicly, they should not be angry with me out of envy, since I wish to do them good.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: caught in argument
lexical_decisions.rationale: The form can mean reasoning or being brought under a syllogistic argument. The context of defeat and being taken unawares favors being caught in argument; reasoning is a material alternative.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐ γὰρ ἡ ἀσθένεια τοῦ ἐκδικοῦντος ἀλήθειά ἐστιν τοῦ νικωμένου
lexical_decisions.chosen: the weakness of its defender is not the truth of the defeated party
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the compact distinction between a weak defender and the truth he defends rather than rewriting it as truth’s weakness.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐ αὐτοῖς διὰ φθόνον ἐμοὶ τῷ εὐεργετεῖν αὐτοὺς θέλοντι χαλεπαίνειν
lexical_decisions.chosen: they should not be angry with me out of envy, since I wish to do them good
lexical_decisions.rationale: Takes αὐτοῖς as the persons for whom getting angry is inappropriate, leaving the grammatical third-person reference intact instead of silently changing it to you, Peter.

lexical_decisions.chosen: to know the Father who is in secret
lexical_decisions.rationale: The secrecy phrase describes the Father, not a secret manner of knowing. This distinction fits Simon’s immediately following public disclosure and agrees with the attributive rendering in 18.6.

passages.text: Peter said, “Since you have spoken in this way to please the crowds present, I will speak not to please them, but truthfully. Tell me: how do you know that everyone present is worthy, when not even one agreed with you as you disclosed it? For their praising me against you is not the act of people agreeing with you, but with me, to whom they also assigned praise as someone who had spoken rightly. But since God, being just, judges each person’s mind, he would not have wished what you say is true to be given to those on the right through the left. By the same reasoning, someone who receives anything from a thief is himself liable. Therefore, for this reason, he did not wish them to receive what you bring, but rather through the Son appointed to reveal. For who can reasonably reveal the Father except the Son alone, since he knows who is worthy of such revelation? Thus this cannot be taught or learned by teaching, but must be revealed by an inexpressible hand to the one worthy to know it.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: to those on the right through the left
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the right/left opposition without identifying unprinted named camps or persons.

lexical_decisions.chosen: by an inexpressible hand
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the hand image, not merely a generic divine act.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τίνι γὰρ εὔλογόν ἐστιν ἀποκαλύπτειν τὸν πατέρα ἢ υἱῷ μόνῳ διὰ τὸ εἰδέναι τῆς τοιαύτης ἀποκαλύψεως τὸν ἄξιον;
lexical_decisions.chosen: For who can reasonably reveal the Father except the Son alone, since he knows who is worthy of such revelation?
lexical_decisions.rationale: τίνι and υἱῷ identify the person for whom revealing is appropriate, thus the revealer. The Son’s preceding appointment and knowledge of worthy recipients confirm this role. The English does not make him the recipient by saying to whom the Father is revealed.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀλλ’ ἐπειδὴ ὁ θεὸς δίκαιος ὢν βραβεύει τὸν ἑκάστου νοῦν, ὃ φῆς ἀληθὲς εἶναι, οὐκ ἂν ἐβουλήθη διὰ τῆς ἀριστερᾶς τοῖς δεξιοῖς τοῦτο δοθῆναι
lexical_decisions.chosen: But since God, being just, judges each person’s mind, he would not have wished what you say is true to be given to those on the right through the left.
lexical_decisions.rationale: Takes ὃ φῆς ἀληθὲς εἶναι as a fronted relative resumed by τοῦτο: the purported truth Simon brings. The subsequent what is brought by you supports this attachment. Alternatively it is parenthetical, which you say is true, modifying the claim that God judges each mind. The printed commas allow both; the revised main text prefers the resumed object without changing the Greek.

passages.text: Simon said, “For a combatant, using his own weapons contributes greatly to victory. For what someone loves he can also genuinely defend, and what is genuinely defended possesses no ordinary strength. Therefore from now on I will set out what I really think. I say that there is a certain power in secrecy, unknown to everyone, even to the maker himself—as Jesus himself also said, without knowing what he uttered; for sometimes, through much talking, someone hits upon the truth without knowing what he says. I am also speaking about this statement he made: ‘No one knew the Father.’” Peter said, “No longer claim to know his teachings.” Simon said, “I do not claim to believe his teachings; I am debating with you about the things he happened to get right.” Peter said, “So as not to give you an excuse to flee, I will discuss with you as you wish. Nevertheless I call everyone to witness that you do not believe even the argument you have now stated. For I know what you think. And so that you do not think I am lying, I will hint at your own views, so that you may see you are conversing with someone who knows.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: what someone loves
lexical_decisions.rationale: The object can be a position or cause, not necessarily a person; this introduces the own-weapons metaphor.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the things he happened to get right
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves Simon’s disparaging account of accidental truth rather than endorsing his claim as a narrator’s assessment.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: λέγω δὲ καὶ περὶ τούτου οὗ εἴρηκεν „οὐδεὶς ἔγνω τὸν πατέρα“.
lexical_decisions.chosen: I am also speaking about this statement he made: No one knew the Father
lexical_decisions.rationale: The main rendering takes τούτου as this statement and οὗ as a relative attracted into the antecedent's genitive case, referring to what he uttered. The surrounding discussion of Jesus' words and the quotation supplying their content favor that reading. A material personal alternative is I am also speaking about this one of whom he said, No one knew the Father, potentially linking the Father to the previously mentioned unknown power. The main text does not claim that this statement rather than a personal referent is uniquely established.

passages.text: “We, Simon, do not say that two angels were sent from the great power, also called the sovereign power, one to create a world and the other to lay down the law. Nor do we say that each came to the things he had made and announced himself as their original author. Nor do we speak of the standing one who will stand as an adversary. Learn how you disbelieve even this hypothesis. The power you say is in secrecy is full of ignorance, for it did not foreknow the ingratitude of the angels it sent.” While Peter was saying this, Simon became very angry and interrupted him, saying, “Why do you babble, you bold man, most reckless of all, plainly disclosing the secrets before uninstructed crowds?” Peter said, “Why do you begrudge the benefit given to the hearers present?” Simon said, “Then do you acknowledge that such knowledge is a benefit?” Peter said, “I do: for once falsehood is known, it gives the benefit of not falling into it through ignorance.” Simon said, “It seems to me that you cannot answer what I put before you. I mean that your teacher too says that there is a certain Father in secrecy.”

source_issues.issue: The nominal clause leaves its finite verbal relation implicit. The main text carries the preceding denial of doctrinal assertion forward; a direct nominal assertion, nor is the standing one going to stand as an adversary, is another grouping. Every surviving element remains.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῆς μεγάλης δυνάμεως, ἔτι τε καὶ τῆς κυρίας λεγομένης
lexical_decisions.chosen: the great power, also called the sovereign power
lexical_decisions.rationale: κυρίας can qualify power as sovereign, ruling, or mistress-like; sovereign power gives its authority sense without adding a separate named deity.

lexical_decisions.chosen: Nor do we speak of the standing one who will stand as an adversary.
lexical_decisions.rationale: The nominal clause is extremely compressed. The main rendering carries do we speak from the preceding repeated denial and preserves standing, future standing, and adversary without supplying a named identity. Nor is the standing one going to stand as an adversary is another possible grouping.

lexical_decisions.chosen: plainly disclosing the secrets
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀτέχνως here means plainly or without qualification, not necessarily in an unskilled manner.

lexical_decisions.chosen: you bold man, most reckless of all
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves both bold and the explicit superlative comparison with all (πάντων), not merely the intensifier utterly.

passages.text: Peter said, “I will answer what you want, concerning ‘No one knew the Father except the Son, nor does anyone know the Son except the Father and those to whom the Son wishes to reveal him.’ First, I am amazed how, when this statement has countless interpretations, you chose the more dangerous part, saying that the statement referred to ignorance on the part of the maker and everyone made by him. For in the first place the statement can have been addressed to all the Jews who supposed David to be the Messiah’s father—with the Messiah himself being the son—and had not recognized him as Son of God. Therefore it was appropriately said, ‘No one knew the Father,’ since everyone named David instead of God. He added, ‘Nor does anyone know the Son,’ because they did not know that he was Son. Saying, ‘Those to whom the Son wishes to reveal him,’ was also rightly said, for the Son who has existed from the beginning alone was appointed to reveal to those he wishes. Thus Adam, the first formed, can have been not ignorant of him; nor can Enoch, who pleased him, fail to know; nor can righteous Noah fail to understand; nor can Abraham the friend fail to comprehend; nor can Isaac have failed to understand; nor can Jacob who wrestled have failed to believe; nor can he have remained unrevealed to all the worthy among the people.”

source_issues.source_quote: καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐν τῷ λαῷ ἀξίοις μὴ ἀποκεκαλύφθαι
source_issues.issue: The final coordination has μὴ but no newly repeated οὐχ. The English carries the previous negative modal scope, nor can ... unrevealed, rather than adding a new printed negation. A clause-local reading would instead yield and not revealed. The modal/negative scope across the entire list is explained in the lexical note on Enoch, Noah, and Abraham.

lexical_decisions.chosen: you chose the more dangerous part
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the comparative, not the unsupported superlative most dangerous.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πρὸς ἀγνωσίαν τοῦ δημιουργοῦ καὶ τῶν ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ πάντων
lexical_decisions.chosen: ignorance on the part of the maker and everyone made by him
lexical_decisions.rationale: The genitives are taken as subjective: maker and created ones are ignorant of the secret Father, as in Simon’s argument. Ignorance of the maker is an objective-genitive alternative, but fits the immediately preceding exchange less well.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐν τῷ λαῷ ἀξίοις μὴ ἀποκεκαλύφθαι
lexical_decisions.chosen: nor can he have remained unrevealed to all the worthy among the people
lexical_decisions.rationale: The final clause is read under the negative modal scope carried from the preceding οὐχ ... μὴ clauses. Its μὴ is retained in unrevealed and the carried denial in nor can. A clause-local reading, and not to have been revealed, remains possible but is less consonant with the preceding argument.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοὺς πατέρα νομίζοντας εἶναι χριστοῦ τὸν Δαυὶδ — καὶ αὐτὸν δὲ τὸν χριστὸν υἱὸν ὄντα — καὶ υἱὸν θεοῦ μὴ ἐγνωκέναι.
lexical_decisions.chosen: who supposed David to be the Messiah’s father—with the Messiah himself being the son—and had not recognized him as Son of God
lexical_decisions.rationale: The printed parenthesis is kept outside the failure-to-recognize phrase and can continue the supposed Davidic father-son relation. It could instead affirm the Messiah’s sonship parenthetically. A broader attachment, taking their failure as not recognizing him as Son and as Son of God, is a material alternative, but the parenthetical punctuation favors keeping the explicit Son-of-God denial as the failed recognition.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐδὲ Ἐνὼχ ὁ εὐαρεστήσας μὴ εἰδέναι οὔτε Νῶε ὁ δίκαιος μὴ ἐπίστασθαι οὔτε Ἀβραὰμ ὁ φίλος μὴ συνιέναι
lexical_decisions.chosen: nor can Enoch ... fail to know; nor can righteous Noah fail to understand; nor can Abraham ... fail to comprehend
lexical_decisions.rationale: The governing δύναται is carried through the list, with οὐδέ/οὔτε denying the modal possibility of each negative-infinitive failure. This gives the explicit nor can ... fail construction. Another reading coordinates the negative infinitival complements under a positive possibility—can be not ignorant, can be not without knowledge—without the same emphasis on exclusion of ignorance. The first Adam clause has only the negative infinitive and is kept as a positive possibility of nonignorance; the later coordinated negatives are made explicit rather than flattened.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐδὲ τὸν υἱόν τις οἶδεν, εἰ μὴ ὁ πατὴρ καὶ οἷς ἂν βούληται ὁ υἱὸς ἀποκαλύψαι
lexical_decisions.chosen: nor does anyone know the Son except the Father and those to whom the Son wishes to reveal him
lexical_decisions.rationale: The object of reveal is unexpressed in Greek. In both quotation occurrences the English him supplies the Father, chosen from the surrounding discussion of the Son revealing the Father, including 18.10. The placement after the exception about knowing the Son also permits the Son or knowledge of his identity as the object of revelation. The Father is therefore an explicitly disclosed contextual choice, not a uniquely printed object; the quotation is not rearranged to match another witness.

passages.text: But if, as you say, he is to be revealed to everyone now through Jesus for the sake of knowing him, how do you not call it most unjust that those men did not know him—seven pillars of the world who were able to please the most just God—while now so many from the nations, impious in every way, know him? Were those men not deemed worthy to know the one better than all? And how is what is not just good? Unless by good you wish to mean not the one who benefits those who have acted justly, but the one who loves the unrighteous even if they do not believe, revealing to them also the secrets that he was unwilling to reveal to the righteous. Such conduct belongs neither to a good nor to a just being, but to one who hates the reverent. Are you perhaps the standing one, Simon, who dares to say these things, which have never been spoken in this way?

lexical_decisions.chosen: seven pillars of the world
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the stated seven without supplying an unprinted list of names.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μήτι σὺ εἶ, Σίμων, ὁ ἑστώς
lexical_decisions.chosen: Are you perhaps the standing one, Simon
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the standing epithet and interrogative challenge, not a translator’s identification of Simon.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰ δὲ (ὡς φῄς) ἔσται διὰ τὸ εἰδέναι διὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ νῦν πᾶσιν ἀποκαλύπτεσθαι:
lexical_decisions.chosen: But if, as you say, he is to be revealed to everyone now through Jesus for the sake of knowing him
lexical_decisions.rationale: Is to be retains future ἔσται while now retains νῦν. The main text construes διὰ τὸ εἰδέναι purposively, for the sake of knowing, with him supplied as the contextual object, the previously discussed Father. The causal alternative is because of knowing; the clause does not state whose prior knowledge would ground disclosure on that attachment. No claim is added that the revealed one was already known to everyone.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὗτοι παντὸς κρείττονος γνῶναι οὐ κατηξιώθησαν;
lexical_decisions.chosen: Were those men not deemed worthy to know the one better than all?
lexical_decisions.rationale: The context concerns knowing the proposed highest Father, favoring a personal referent superior to all and παντός as the comparison of κρείττονος. Taking παντός with substantival κρείττονος gives the broader alternative Were these not deemed worthy to know anything superior? The genitive superior object is construed with deemed worthy/knowing in this compressed phrase; the personal interpretation is not claimed as unique.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μήτι σὺ εἶ, Σίμων, ὁ ἑστώς, ὁ ταῦτα οὕτως μήποτε ῥηθέντα εἰπεῖν ἀποθρασυνόμενος;
lexical_decisions.chosen: Are you perhaps the standing one, Simon, who dares to say these things, which have never been spoken in this way?
lexical_decisions.rationale: The things never spoken in this way are the object of Simon’s audacious saying. The phrase does not state that Simon himself claims they were previously spoken; the English does not introduce that unsupported reported-speech proposition.

passages.text: Indignant at this, Simon said, “I accuse your teacher, who said, ‘I give thanks to you, Lord of heaven and earth, because the things that were hidden from the wise you revealed to nursing infants.’” Peter said, “That is not how the statement was spoken. But first I will speak as though it had been said as you supposed. Even if our Lord had said, ‘The things that were hidden from the wise, these the Father revealed to infants,’ he would not even in this way have been understood to indicate a God and Father other than the one who created the world. For the hidden things he spoke of can belong to the maker himself, since Isaiah also said, ‘I will open my mouth in parables and pour out things hidden from the foundation of the world.’ Do you therefore acknowledge the prophet who was not ignorant of the hidden things that Jesus says were concealed from the wise but revealed to infants? How, then, was the maker ignorant when his prophet Isaiah was not ignorant? But our Jesus in fact did not say, ‘The things that were hidden,’ but spoke what seems harsher; for he said, ‘You revealed them to nursing infants.’ But saying, ‘You hid,’ refers to things once known to them. For the key of the kingdom of the heavens lay with them, that is, knowledge of the secrets.”

source_issues.issue: The formerly selected fragment was σμέων, yielding ἔγνω σμέων; independently blind-checked print evidence now reads the physical line-start fragment σμένων, correcting the omitted ν. The print still divides ἔγνω / σμένων without a hyphen. The English tests their combined perfect-passive participial reading, not a uniquely certified analysis or replacement Greek. The blind receipt describes the initial ε diacritic as tentatively smooth breathing plus acute, less distinct than the letters, while the following fragment has acute on ε; this anomalous accent/division is preserved as a disclosed print feature. No original letters beyond the independently verified ν are invented.

The current selected text reads ἀπέκρυψας, rendered You hid. The blind fragment-check response’s incidental full-line transcription instead reports ἀπεκάλυψας at this quote position. The authorized curation only verifies σμένων, so that incidental quote reading is not adopted or silently substituted here.
